source.title_on_document: Sequential Human-AI Collaboration Impairs Narrative Creativity in University Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial

supplement.where: Research Square supplementary files listed on p. 20: DataSPSS.sav and researchtools.pdf (download links, no URL printed). Data Availability (p. 12) says datasets and materials will be in the supplementary files.
supplement.holds: The participant-level data file (DataSPSS.sav) and the research tools (researchtools.pdf). The main text has no table of outcome means, SDs, or per-arm analyzed ns after Cook's-distance exclusions; those would have to come from the data file.

paper_design_summary: 112 undergraduate students at Yangzhou University were randomly assigned to one of four conditions for a two-stage story-writing task ('Imagine and depict the future world', 15 minutes per draft): AI-first (AI on the first draft, final draft alone), AI-follow (first draft alone, AI on the final draft), AI-parallel (AI on both drafts), or Human-only (no AI). Participants chose their own chatbot (e.g., ChatGPT, DeepSeek). Both drafts were scored for creativity (originality, fluency, flexibility, elaboration on 9-point scales) by 10 trained student raters and by DeepSeek-V3; the main analysis is an ANCOVA of final-draft creativity controlling for first-draft creativity and covariates, with Human-only as reference.

studies.label: Two-stage narrative story-writing RCT with four collaboration conditions

arms.name: AI-first

arms.name: AI-follow

participants.exclusions: The paper reports only the count after 'data screening for attrition and non-compliance' (112 valid cases, arms 28/25/30/29); the number assigned before screening and the number dropped are not stated. Five participants (4.5%) had missing values, handled by multiple imputation (MICE, five datasets), 'yielding a final sample of N = 112 for all analyses' (p. 7). Influential cases were then excluded model by model with Cook's distance (D > 4/n): 7 cases in the human-rated ANCOVA (F(3, 96), implying 105 analyzed), 8 in the AI-rated ANCOVA (F(3, 95), implying 104), unstated numbers in the subdomain ANCOVAs, and 10 in the self-efficacy ANCOVA (N = 102). Per-arm counts after these exclusions are not reported. Not an intention-to-treat analysis.
participants.who: Undergraduate students at Yangzhou University from the humanities, social sciences, STEM, agriculture, and medicine; required to have experience using GenAI tools and no language or writing impairments; mean age 19.47 (SD 1.20); 64 male across arms (16+17+17+14). Performance-based pay of 25 to 45 CNY.
participants.country: Not stated explicitly; Yangzhou University, pay in CNY
participants.quote: Following data screening for attrition and non-compliance, 112 valid cases remained, resulting in a total of 224 creative writing samples (first and final drafts combined).
participants.locator: p. 4, Section 2.1; p. 7, Section 2.5; p. 8, Section 3.1 and Table 1

ai_tool.name_model: Participant's choice of generative AI tool, e.g., ChatGPT or DeepSeek (specific models not recorded)
ai_tool.how_used: In AI-assisted stages participants could use any tool such as ChatGPT or DeepSeek, send prompts freely, and adopt or reject AI-generated content (pp. 5 and 7). Interaction modes were not controlled or categorized (p. 11).

task.description: Open-ended narrative story on the prompt 'Imagine and depict the future world'; a first draft and then a final draft, with the first draft available for reference but not editable in the final stage. Instructions asked for novelty, idea richness, diverse perspectives, detail, coherence, and completeness, with pay tied to ratings.
task.duration: Two stages of 15 minutes each (first draft, final draft)

outcomes.name: Human-rated overall narrative creativity of the final draft, AI available at the final stage (AI-follow and AI-parallel vs Human-only)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Ten trained undergraduate raters (coursework in innovation or entrepreneurship, university creativity awards), blind to condition; each narrative rated by all ten on originality, fluency, flexibility, and elaboration (9-point scales). ICC 0.722 in formal evaluation. How the overall score is formed from the four dimensions is not stated. ANCOVA ('robust ANCOVA') of final-draft score on group dummies, controlling for first-draft score, age, gender, AI literacy, creative personality; 7 influential cases excluded by Cook's distance (F(3, 96) implies 105 analyzed). Adjusted means reported.

contrasts.reported: Omnibus F(3, 96) = 9.62, p < .001, partial eta^2 = .38. Adjusted means: Human-only M = 5.65, SE = 0.10; AI-follow M = 4.81, SE = 0.10; p < .001, d = -1.41
Adjusted means: Human-only M = 5.65, SE = 0.10; AI-parallel M = 5.17, SE = 0.10; p = .262, d = -0.33 (not significant)

data_and_code.data_url: Research Square supplementary file DataSPSS.sav listed on p. 20 (no URL printed); preprint DOI https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-8774138/v1

eligibility.reason: Students were randomly assigned to three generative-AI collaboration conditions or a no-AI control (p. 4, Section 2.1). 112 people were analyzed (105 in the main human-rated ANCOVA after 7 Cook's-distance exclusions), well above 50; the count at assignment before screening for attrition and non-compliance is not reported. Outcomes are creativity ratings of the stories by blind human raters and by DeepSeek-V3. The AI-follow and AI-parallel contrasts answer with_ai; the AI-first contrast scores a final draft written without AI and answers after_ai.

one_line_finding: Adjusted human-rated final-draft creativity was 5.65 (SE 0.10) for Human-only versus 4.86 for AI-first (d = -0.95, p = .002), 4.81 for AI-follow (d = -1.41, p < .001), and 5.17 for AI-parallel (d = -0.33, p = .262), from an ANCOVA controlling for first-draft creativity (p. 8, Section 3.2).
open_questions: The ANCOVA controls for first-draft creativity, but in AI-first and AI-parallel the first draft was itself written with AI, so the covariate is post-treatment. The 'baseline imbalance' the paper attributes to sampling variability (p. 7) may partly be a treatment effect; the AI-first and AI-parallel final-draft contrasts are adjusted for it.
Number of people assigned before 'data screening for attrition and non-compliance' is not reported, nor how many were dropped per arm (p. 4).

Cook's-distance exclusions are made model by model (7 human-rated, 8 AI-rated, unstated for subdomains); per-arm analyzed counts after exclusions are not reported. Sample sizes for the main contrasts come from the F degrees of freedom (105 and 104).
The standardizer for the reported Cohen's d is not stated; adjusted means are given with SEs, not SDs.
Section 3.4 (subdomains) does not say whether the scores are human or AI ratings; coded as human ratings. Figures 3 and 4 show both.
How the overall creativity score combines the four dimensions is not stated.
AI-first final drafts were written without AI but revise an AI-assisted first draft that participants could consult; coded after_ai with immediate timing per the codebook rule.
The post hoc power analysis mentions two covariates (p. 4), while the model has first-draft score plus four covariates (p. 8).
notes: Creative self-efficacy (17-item self-report, pre and post) is also analyzed: no significant group effect, F(3, 93) = 2.29, p = .083, N = 102 after excluding 10 influential cases (p. 9, Section 3.5). It is self-reported, so it is not listed as an outcome. No diversity-across-people outcome is reported. Subdomain results for AI ratings appear only in Figure 4 (p. 19), without tests; they are not listed separately. Human raters were trained undergraduate students, coded human_raters rather than expert_raters. Missing values for 5 participants were multiply imputed (MICE, five datasets).
